html:
SMTO-CTR-0005 — An attached file no longer matches what SMTO recorded

GUID: 63074936-6aa1-48d9-8960-6fdf2340e304
Slug: task-contract-context-metadata-mismatch
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • When you sent the request, SMTO noted each attached file's name, type and size. One of them now looks different, so SMTO didn't act on this version of your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the files attached to the original request and decide which version you want SMTO to use. SMTO won't guess which file you meant once its details no longer match.
  2. Send the request again as a new message and attach that file again with Add context. A new request records the file's details as they are now, so they match.
  3. Don't keep selecting Retry on the old task. Retry reuses the file details SMTO recorded earlier, so it stops at the same mismatch.

What success looks like

  • The new task shows Task contract generated and starts working with the file you attached.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep retrying the old task; it will stop at the same check each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Saved Task Contract context metadata (source type, name, media type or byte count) disagrees with the current context source, or an offline contract reference disagrees with its manifest entry.

What this means

  • Saved context metadata disagrees with current source type/name/media type/byte count, or offline contract references disagree with their manifest metadata. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Saved context metadata disagrees with current source type/name/media type/byte count, or offline contract references disagree with their manifest metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact context ID and metadata fields; separate admission manifest checks from offline contract diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Compare the context_id's entry in the run's available_context_manifest with the current ContextStore metadata (source kind, name, media_type, bytes); for offline checks, compare the contract's authoritative_references with the supplied manifest. Start a new request that captures the intended source again rather than retrying with the stale manifest.
  • Refresh and review the authoritative context metadata before recompiling or rerunning the offline check.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported flow uses authoritative matching source metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
